findings.description: `host.endswith(domain)` has no label boundary. With partner domain `shop.example`, an origin such as `https://evilshop.example` or `https://attacker-shop.example` passes. The policy then reflects that origin with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. A hostile site can then read the member's balance and POST redemptions using the member's session cookie.
findings.suggestion: Accept only an exact match or a true subdomain: `host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain)`.
findings.title: Partner domain suffix match lacks a dot boundary, so attacker-controlled domains are allowed with credentials

findings.description: `parts.hostname` drops the port and userinfo. An origin like `https://user@partner.example:8443` or one with an arbitrary port is accepted as a partner origin, and the raw string is reflected back. This is looser than the exact-origin matching and widens the trusted set to any port on the partner host.
findings.suggestion: Reject origins where `parts.username`, `parts.password` or `parts.port` are set, or compare the netloc to the hostname.
findings.title: Origin with port or userinfo is not validated beyond hostname
